panels.title: A. Depth check — distinct series available for THIS ONE VM

panels.description: Every distinct time series (metric name x label combination) currently scraped for this VMI. Multi-instance metrics (per-vCPU, per-vNIC, per-drive) each contribute one series per instance — this is the honest Prometheus definition of 'series', not 'metric names'.
panels.title: kubevirt_vmi_* series (VMI-scoped)

panels.description: Adds VM-level series (kubevirt_vm_info, kubevirt_vm_resource_requests/limits, kubevirt_vm_disk_allocated_size_bytes, kubevirt_vm_labels, lifecycle timestamps) that exist even while the VM is stopped.
panels.title: + kubevirt_vm_* series (VM object, incl. stopped-state)

panels.description: THE ACTUAL COMPARISON POINT. Joins on the virt-launcher pod's kube-state-metrics label vm.kubevirt.io/name=<vm> (a real label, not an ownerReference — see Korrel8r note below) to pull in every standard cAdvisor container_* and kube-state-metrics kube_pod_* series for that VM's compute pod: cgroup CPU/mem/network/PSI-if-enabled, restart counts, resource requests/limits, node placement, etc. This is what 'same open store, joinable by ordinary labels' means concretely.

targets.expr:
(count({namespace="$namespace", name="$vm", __name__=~"kubevirt_(vmi|vm)_.*"}) or vector(0))
+
(count(
  {namespace="$namespace", __name__=~"container_.*|kube_pod_.*"}
  * on(namespace,pod) group_left()
  (kube_pod_labels{namespace="$namespace", label_vm_kubevirt_io_name="$vm"} * 0 + 1)
) or vector(0))

panels.title: + virt-launcher pod series (container_*, kube_pod_*)

options.content:
**Do not present this as "we expose more metrics than vCenter."**

vCenter/Aria expose a **fixed counter set per statistics level (1-4)** — it does not grow or shrink per VM the way a label-indexed TSDB does, so a raw side-by-side count is apples-to-oranges and an architect will call it out.

The defensible claim is narrower and stronger: **every one of these series is independently queryable, joinable by arbitrary label, and reachable with ordinary PromQL — right now, with no SDK, no vRealize add-on, no PowerCLI script.** Lead with that sentence, not the number.

panels.title: Read this before you show it
B. Standard CPU / memory / network / storage (parity with vCenter — same open store)

panels.description: No prerequisite. kubevirt_vmi_cpu_usage_seconds_total = vcpu + hypervisor time, counter.
panels.title: vCPU usage (all modes)

panels.description: Recording rule. No prerequisite.
panels.title: Allocated vCPUs

panels.description: No prerequisite (both are hypervisor/cgroup-level, agentless).
panels.title: Domain memory vs virt-launcher working set

panels.description: No prerequisite. Verify the `interface` label exists in your build via the preflight script — if it does not, drop the `by (interface)` grouping.
panels.title: Network throughput by interface

panels.description: No prerequisite.
panels.title: Network errors / drops

panels.description: No prerequisite. Verify the `drive` label via preflight. ⚠ KubeVirt's own e2e coverage for storage read/write bytes was flaky/quarantined in CI (Aug 2026), timing-correlated with a fix that skips domain-stats collection during live migration — expect possible gaps in this panel during the migration beat below.
panels.title: Storage IOPS + throughput by drive
C. Signals with NO vCenter/Aria equivalent (Section 2.2 / 5 of the research)

panels.description: Native histogram, no prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: vCenter has only raw create/power-on Get-VIEvent timestamps, no distribution. NOTE: a single VM rarely generates enough samples for a meaningful quantile alone — for the live demo, drop the {name="$vm"} filter to show the FLEET distribution, then point at this VM's individual transition on the timeline.
panels.title: Phase-transition latency (creation → phase), p50/p95/p99

panels.description: No prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: Aria's disk set (IOPS, latency, outstanding/queued) has no cache-flush counter at all.
panels.title: Storage flush (fsync) rate + derived avg flush latency

panels.description: No prerequisite. PARTIAL vs VMware: Aria has Consumed/Balloon%/Guest Free/Needed — a different model, no 1:1 mapping. Not accurate if the guest OS hasn't initialized all assigned pages.
panels.title: Memory available vs usable (balloon-adjusted)

panels.description: REQUIRES qemu-guest-agent >= 10.0.0 in the guest. GAP vs VMware: VMware Tools does not expose a load average even when installed — no panel, silently blank, if the agent isn't present or is older.
panels.title: Guest OS load average (qemu-guest-agent)

panels.description: REQUIRES the schedstats=enable kernel argument applied cluster-wide via a worker MachineConfig. With no MachineConfig applied this panel is SILENTLY BLANK — no error, just 'No data'. CLOSE vs VMware: Aria CPU Ready % (delay) / CPU Other Wait ms (wait).
panels.title: vCPU delay + wait (scheduler contention / I/O wait)

panels.description: No prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: no native guest kernel-panic/BSOD counter in vCenter/Aria; closest is HA heartbeat monitoring. Alert: VMNonRecoverableOSPanic / ClusterVMPanicDetected (verified in kubevirt/monitoring runbooks).
panels.title: guest_os_panic (24h)

panels.description: No prerequisite (boolean gauge; only meaningful if evictionStrategy: LiveMigrate is set on the VM). GAP vs VMware: no equivalent gauge. Alert: VMCannotBeEvicted (verified runbook).
panels.title: non_evictable (live-migration blocked)

panels.description: No prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: vCenter logs console-access events but exposes no rolled-up idle/security gauge.
panels.title: Time since last console/VNC/SSH connection

panels.description: No prerequisite. Cluster-wide gauge, not scoped to a single VM (shown here for fleet context after a CNV upgrade). GAP vs VMware: architecturally no analog; closest is VMware Tools version status. Alert: OutdatedVirtualMachineInstanceWorkloads (verified runbook).
panels.title: Fleet-wide: VMIs on outdated virt-launcher
D. Live migration beat — trigger `virtctl migrate $vm` and watch it happen

options.content:
```bash
virtctl migrate $vm -n $namespace
# or, to name the VirtualMachineInstanceMigration object explicitly:
oc create -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: kubevirt.io/v1
kind: VirtualMachineInstanceMigration
metadata:
  generateName: $vm-migration-
  namespace: $namespace
spec:
  vmiName: $vm
EOF
```
Then flip this row's time range to 'Last 5 minutes' with 5s refresh and watch the panels below move live.

panels.title: Trigger command (run in terminal, not in Grafana)

panels.description: No prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: vSphere shows only an ephemeral % progress bar during the migration and nothing after — this is a queryable, historically-retained time series.
panels.title: Live migration data processed vs remaining

panels.description: No prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: vSphere 8 gives total MB moved AFTER completion, not a live rate.
panels.title: Live memory transfer rate

panels.description: No prerequisite. Cluster-wide queue depth, not scoped to $vm — this is what makes it a real queue, not a per-migration progress bar. GAP vs VMware: Aria counts COMPLETED vMotions per host; no live queue.
panels.title: Migration queue depth by phase (cluster-wide)

panels.description: Native histogram, no prerequisite. GAP vs VMware: vSphere 8 vMotion counters give one point value per migration, no distribution across the fleet.
panels.title: Migration phase-transition latency, p95 (live)

panels.description: ⚠ OPEN BUG CNV-94992: kubevirt_vmi_dirty_rate_bytes_per_second has been measured off by 2-3 orders of magnitude vs ground truth. Show this panel ONLY as a directional trend line (is it rising or falling), never read a number off it out loud, and disclose the bug if asked. vSphere never surfaces this counter at all — ESXi uses it internally for vMotion convergence decisions but does not expose it — so even a buggy version is more than VMware shows, but frame it as 'this is the metric we're actively fixing,' not a win.
panels.title: ⚠ Dirty-memory rate — KNOWN ACCURACY BUG, do not quote absolute values

options.content:
KubeVirt's own e2e tests for storage read/write bytes and **flush requests/times** were flaky/quarantined in CI (Aug 2026), timing-correlated with a fix that **skips domain-stats collection during live migration**.

**Translation for the demo:** the Row B storage IOPS/throughput panels for *this VM* may flatten or gap for a few seconds while the migration in this row is in flight. That is a known, disclosed limitation — do not let it read as a broken dashboard live.

panels.title: Storage-metric caveat during this migration window
E. Slice by ANY label, fleet-wide — no PowerCLI scripting required

panels.description: Slice by NODE. No prerequisite. Verify the `node` label is present on virt-handler-sourced VMI metrics in your build via the preflight script; if absent, join via kube_pod_info{node=...} on the virt-launcher pod instead.
panels.title: Top 5 nodes by VM vCPU usage

panels.description: Slice by NAMESPACE. Recording rule, no prerequisite. A vCenter admin gets this from a Folder/Resource Pool view configured in advance; here it is one label on an ad hoc query against any metric.
panels.title: VM count by namespace, fleet-wide

panels.description: Slice by INSTANCETYPE LABEL. Verify the `instance_type` label on kubevirt_vmi_info in your build via the preflight script (recent KubeVirt versions add it; not guaranteed on every build). No vCenter equivalent — instance types/preferences are a KubeVirt-native concept.
panels.title: VM count by instance type, fleet-wide

panels.description: Slice by a label YOU put on the VM object (here: `team`). Requires the label to be allow-listed in the 'kubevirt-vm-labels-config' ConfigMap so kubevirt_vm_labels exposes it as label_team. Replace 'team' with your own key (e.g. cost_center, environment, owner). This join — arbitrary business label to live usage — is exactly the PowerCLI-scripting case for a vCenter admin; here it is one PromQL join.
panels.title: CPU usage grouped by a USER-DEFINED VM label

panels.description: TOP-K across the fleet, not scoped to $namespace/$vm on purpose. No prerequisite. Swap the metric for cpu_usage_seconds_total, storage_iops_*, or memory_usable_bytes for other fleet-wide leaderboards — same one-line pattern every time.
panels.title: Top 10 VMs fleet-wide by network transmit
